newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Esso Malaysia begins output from Lawit gas field.
newsitem.headline: Esso Malaysia begins output from Lawit gas field.

text.p: Esso Production Malaysia Inc, a division of Exxon Corp, said on Wednesday that it had started production and sales from the Lawit gas field offshore Malaysia's eastern Terengganu state.

Philip Dingle, chairman and chief executive officer of Esso, said in a statement that by 1999 Lawit would be capable of supplying about one-third of Peninsular Malaysia's gas requirements and help meet the growing demand for natural gas in the country.

The 1.5 billion ringgit Lawit field development is Esso's second major gas project in Malaysia, after the Jerneh gas field, under the natural gas project and sales agreement with state oil company, Petronas.
Sales of Jerneh gas began in 1992.
The Lawit development drilling, which involves 17 wells, started in January this year.

With the planned completion of the drilling programme by the end of this year, the average daily production from the field is expected to reach about 450 million standard cubic feet per day (mcfd), Dingle said.

Compression facilities will be installed in 1998 to increase production from Lawit to its design capacity of 700 mcfd. This will increase Esso's gas delivery capacity to nearly 1.6 billion cubic feet per day from its current capacity of 900 mcfd, he said.
Dingle said the development of Lawit was a significant milestone as it would further allow the country to use its natural gas resources and fuel its development.
